critical_code_review_comments: search_router.py routes via rbac.can(role, perm, 'read'). Perm 'hr_advances' is currently open to all roles — this leaks employee_advances into low-privilege palettes. Consider a stricter perm or explicit role-list per registry entry.

search_router.py catches broad Exception in _search_one() and returns None silently; a per-collection failure would be invisible. Consider logging.warning so ops can spot misconfigured collections/indexes.

No per-user rate limiting on /api/search — palette debounces at ~180ms client-side but a malicious caller could fan out 55 concurrent regex scans per request. Consider a small text-index or index on high-cardinality fields (po_number, invoice_no, name) for performance at scale.

rca_of_the_issue: RBAC leak — sales_executive sees 'employee_advances' in /api/search results. Root cause: /app/backend/rbac.py line 467-472 defines hr_advances.read = {'*'} (wildcard). The search router filters registry entries with rbac.can(role, entry.perm, 'read'), so every collection whose perm is a wildcard-read leaks to every logged-in role. Reproduction: (1) POST /api/auth/login {sales@erp.com/Sales@123}, (2) GET /api/search?q=arjun, (3) observe groups[].key includes 'employee_advances'. Mitigation options: (a) tighten hr_advances.read to a role list ({super_admin, hr_executive, accounts_executive, general_manager, director, dept_head}), or (b) add a per-registry allow_roles/deny_roles field in search_router.REGISTRY that layers on top of rbac.can().
